reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a flash-loan arbitrage scheme that asks viewers to connect or use a wallet, send liquidity or gas money to a deployed contract, and execute the process. It claims that the transaction will automatically repay the amount and return profit within seconds or minutes, while presenting the method as repeatable.

citations.quote: You need to deposit at least 0.1 per 1000 borrowed for the contract to execute correctly and complete the flash loan uniswap bot.
any profit remaining will be transferred to your wallet.
This will connect to your metamask wallet so that you can interact with the contract
Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.
click the red Action button and confirm the gas fees to execute the flash loan attack.

opening.argument: The material includes an explicit risk warning that flash-loan exploits have been used against vulnerable DeFi protocols. That warning gives the presentation a cautionary, risk-aware character rather than certifying that every transaction will succeed. The instructions also acknowledge operational uncertainty: the speaker says that without funding, the action would not work, and recommends avoiding underfunding. A careful viewer is therefore being shown a risky process with conditions and hazards, not promised a risk-free outcome.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and get millions of dollars.
if I were to accidentally grand the action without giving a gas money it would have done anything
it's better to over fund it than under fund it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the funding instructions as proof of deception, but funding and gas are ordinary prerequisites for a blockchain demonstration. Its selected quotes do not establish that the creator concealed risks or guaranteed success. The description itself expressly warns that flash-loan exploits have attacked vulnerable protocols, which is inconsistent with portraying the process as risk-free.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and get millions of dollars.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is a brief contextual statement, not a warning that viewers may lose their funds or that this particular contract is unsafe. The argument's own citations confirm that viewers are told to fund a contract and proceed. A generic reference to past exploits does not neutralize instructions to deposit liquidity and execute the action.

confirm the gas fees to execute the flash loan attack.

opening.argument: The central activity is an operational programming tutorial: it directs the viewer through Remix, a Solidity file, compiler selection, deployment, wallet connection, and contract interaction. The supplied frames likewise show the Remix development environment, Solidity code, deployment controls, and wallet interface. The speaker presents a reproducible technical workflow, including how to create a file and compile code, rather than merely asking viewers to trust a sales claim. The stated subject is implementation of a flash-loan smart contract and arbitrage process.

citations.quote: First you have to go to Remix. This is where we're gonna write the smart contract
Copy and paste the contract code into the new file
Choose the compiler that matches the top of the code
you'll have your contract before we can run the contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not change what the tutorial tells viewers to do. The instructions move beyond explaining code: they direct viewers to connect a wallet, send liquidity to a newly deployed contract, and confirm an action framed as an attack. The educational format therefore functions as the delivery mechanism for the proposed transaction.

citations.quote: This will connect to your metamask wallet so that you can interact with the contract
send the liquidity to the new contract code
confirm the gas fees to execute the flash loan attack.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical steps are not neutral classroom code exercises. They instruct a viewer to create and fund a contract, execute it, and expect funds to return with profit. The argument identifies the format, but its citations do not show testing, code review, or a detached explanation; they show deployment and execution instructions tied to financial returns.

citations.quote: any profit remaining will be transferred to your wallet.
Wait until the transaction is confirmed on the blockchain
That's it! The flash loan will be paid back automatically

opening.argument: The supplied record does not establish that the creator received money, controlled a viewer's wallet, or completed a transfer on a viewer's behalf. It presents a software workflow involving publicly described tools: Remix, MetaMask, Ethereum, and Uniswap. The material identifies the process as arbitrage and explains that gas is needed for transactions. Even though it discusses depositing liquidity, the record does not identify a recipient, verify the contract's ownership, or prove that any viewer's funds were taken. Those missing facts leave an ordinary software-service or instructional interpretation open.

citations.quote: Remix Website: https://remixcompiler.com/
To get started, you need to have MetaMask browser extension installed.
You're going to have to send gas money to run this contract.
The flash loan will be paid back automatically and any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.

rebuttal.rebuttal: This is not merely ordinary software promotion. The viewer is told to deposit liquidity into a new contract and confirm a transaction called the action. The promised mechanism is explicit: the contract is said to repay the loan and return profit. The absence of a named recipient or proven completed transfer does not make those solicitations ordinary or safe.

citations.quote: send the liquidity to the new contract code
confirm the gas fees to execute the flash loan attack
any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-recipient point is not decisive because the instructions still direct the viewer to send liquidity to a newly deployed contract and fund gas. More importantly, the material pairs those deposits with repeated profit-oriented claims, including that higher liquidity produces higher profit. A missing proof of an actual completed transfer does not remove the solicitation mechanism.

citations.quote: The more you deposit, the more swaps can be performed in the flash loan arbitrage.
any profit remaining will be transferred to your wallet.
The higher the liquidity, the higher the profit
